business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vapor Deposition of Amorphous Silicon Cesium Iodide DR Detectors

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with a unitary federal company-law code and decentralized cantonal commercial-registry administration
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China–Switzerland Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 July 2014)
Switzerland–China Double Taxation Convention of 6 July 1966, as amended by the Protocol signed 25 September 2013 (Protocol in force 5 October 2016)
Swiss network of more than 100 in-force Bilateral Investment Treaties providing ISDS and MFN/NT protections

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Art. 620 et seq. (Aktienrecht) and Art. 697j–697m (statutory register of beneficial owners); Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) with its implementing Ordinance (AMLO, SR 955.01); FINMA AML circulars and Banking Act confidentiality duties; Federal Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO sanctions ordinances; Handelsregisterverordnung (HRegV, SR 221.411).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial public deed of incorporation and executed Articles of Association (Statuten)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal Notary (Notariat) of the registered-office canton
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic use: no apostille; executed before Swiss notary and filed at the Cantonal Commercial Register Office; foreign use: Hague Apostille by the Cantonal State Chancellery under SR 211.213.01

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certified Extract from the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterauszug)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), retrievable via ZEFIX
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille applied by the Cantonal State Chancellery for foreign judicial, banking, and licensing authorities; Consular Legalization by the receiving Swiss/foreign embassy for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identity documents, residence certificates, and proof of address of all founders and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing police/immigration authority in country of origin; Swiss notary certifies conformity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of notarized copies originating from non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign parent/shareholder Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign competent companies/registry authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the foreign competent authority; if a non-Hague state, Consular Legalization by the Swiss Embassy or Consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence: all founders, UBOs, directors and authorized signatories must be screened against (i) the Swiss PEP regime under the AMLA (politically exposed persons and their close associates/family), (ii) the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, (iii) Swiss SECO-implemented sanctions and embargo measures under SR 946.231, (iv) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and (v) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists as the prevailing CFT standard of Swiss private banks. Screening must be evidenced pre-incorporation, refreshed on a 90-day cycle, and archived in the corporate KYC file; positive hits require a written Swiss attorney opinion and may require prior consent escalation to the bank or MROS.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX – Zentraler Firmenindex / Swiss Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP); name applications are filed at the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (e.g., Handelsregisteramt Zürich, Zug, or Geneva) following a preliminary name examination (Vorabprüfung).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must comply with Art. 950 OR: the name may be in German, French, Italian, or a Latin-script combination; foreign-language designations must be transliterated into Latin characters and may not include ideographs or pictograms; the name must contain the statutory legal-form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German) / 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' (French); the name must be truthful, non-misleading, and sufficiently distinct from all existing registered names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Switzerland / Swissness (Art. 47–49 Trade Mark Protection Act – prior federal approval and proven local commercial substance required)
Bank / Banque / Banker (prior FINMA banking licence mandatory)
Insurance / Assurance / Versicherung (prior FINMA supervisory licence mandatory)
Federal / Eidgenössisch / Federal Government (prior FDJP authorization required)
Trust / Treuhand / Fiduciaire (cantonal registration and licensing may be required)
Cantonal, municipal, or sovereign emblems (strict authorization rules)
Medical / Pharma / Radiology / Diagnostic terms capable of misleading regarding a health-care or medical-device licence (Swissmedic assessment advisable)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The Cantonal Commercial Register Office issues a preliminary name-examination confirmation that reserves the name for 180 days; extensions may be granted upon written request where incorporation intent is evidenced. If the name is rejected, the office must issue an appealable decree (Verfügung); the applicant may file an administrative appeal (Rekurs) within 30 days of service to the cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority, attaching an alternative name proposal; further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court and ultimately to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual-office or mail-forwarding address is not accepted as sufficient registered-office substance for an active medical-device OEM (ISIC 3250 digital X-ray flat-panel detector manufacturing). The AG must maintain a verifiable seat and central administration in Switzerland in accordance with Art. 623 OR, with corporate books, minutes, and management functions locally present. A virtual service address may satisfy formal registration in certain cantons for holding entities, but Swissmedic/GMP, ISO 13485, banking KYC, and VAT/export compliance for radiology hardware require physical premises and supervised local substance; a leased Swiss office with operational personnel in the registered canton is the market norm.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 20% risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first 12 months post-incorporation, reflecting (i) Swissmedic and notified-body ISO 13485/medical-device audits, (ii) commercial-register address-verification checks, and (iii) Swiss bank AML/UBO physical-visit protocols at account opening; long-run annualized likelihood is 10–15% for an unquoted Low_Risk_Standard manufacturing entity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance (Vorabprüfung) and 180-day name reservation at the Cantonal Commercial Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of the registered-office canton

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and drafting of Articles of Association (Statuten) for an AG with CHF 100,000 minimum capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff graduated on subscribed capital; market benchmark CHF 1,200–2,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Register registration of the AG, including publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and SOGC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee (CHF 500–1,200 by capital) plus gazette publication fee (approx. CHF 60–100)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Establishment of the statutory register of beneficial owners and shareholder ledger (UBO register per Art. 697j–697m OR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Swiss legal counsel or licensed fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for private company corporate-housekeeping setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory PEP, UN, SECO, EU, and OFAC sanctions screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories (initial annual subscription)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription benchmark for Swiss screening databases

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence: shareholder and UBO structure review, corporate-purpose analysis for ISIC 3250, Swissmedic licensing pathway, and shareholders' agreement drafting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss law firm or licensed fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Time-based market rate benchmark (CHF 350–600/hour) with fixed-fee assessment

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign corporate documents (e.g., parent-company resolutions and certificates) into the official cantonal language (German or French)
Apostille / consular legalization bundle for foreign shareholder and UBO identity packages (2 to 4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authority, Cantonal State Chancellery, and Swiss Embassy/Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague apostille tariff per document plus consular service fees for non-Hague jurisdictions

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/SR 220), Articles 620-763, in particular Articles 626-629 (incorporation), 632 (minimum capital), 628 (content of articles of association), and 640 (registration in the Commercial Register).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) in the canton of registered office, supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Authority (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration to the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung im Handelsregister) accompanied by the notarially certified articles of association, list of directors, specimen signatures, declaration of paid-up capital, and bank confirmation of escrowed funds.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital for an Aktiengesellschaft is CHF 100,000. At least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid up in cash into a blocked escrow account before registration, with an absolute minimum of CHF 50,000 paid-up capital. The paid-up funds must be confirmed by a Swiss bank in a capital release statement (Depotschein) and must remain at the free disposal of the board after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE AKTIENGESELLSCHAFT: The board unanimously resolves that (1) the share subscriptions stated in the notarial deed are approved, the subscribers are admitted as shareholders, and the paid-up escrowed capital is accepted as being at the company's free disposal; (2) the registered office is adopted at the address designated in the articles of association and the board is authorised to occupy such office; (3) the elected directors are formally appointed, with [Name] elected as Chairperson and [Name] appointed as Delegated Officer or sole signatory as specified in the articles; (4) the Chairperson is authorised to execute the Commercial Register application and to undertake all ancillary registration and licensing filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Drafting of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Independent cantonal notary (Notariat) in cooperation with the intended Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of association in accordance with OR Articles 626-628, including company name, objects, share capital, registered office, share classes, and management provisions. Gather founder identification and beneficial ownership declarations. Submit the draft to the chosen notary for preliminary legal review. The notary will require all proposed registered office and Swiss legal address details to be confirmed.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry raises a deficiency, amend the draft articles and re-submit with a written explanatory note; no additional filing fee is normally charged for preliminary advisory corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in the canton of the company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange a physical execution meeting before the notary for all incorporators. The notary certifies the signatures, verifies the identities, and formally executes the articles of association. The notarial deed must contain express acceptance of the share subscription and declaration that the board members have been elected.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if any, for founder representation
Notary engagement letter and fee agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is queried, the notary will issue a formal deficiency note; the incorporators must cure the issue by supplemental declaration or a revised execution meeting, with no loss of priority if cured within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Escrow Capital Account and Depositing Minimum Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or FINMA-licensed financial intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital escrow account (Aktienkapitalkonto) in the name of the company, expressly for the incorporation subscription proceeds. Deposit at least 20% of each share's nominal value, in any case at least CHF 50,000. The bank issues a capital release confirmation certifying the funds are available and free of claims or set-off rights.
required_dossiers: Company address and business purpose details
Founder and beneficial owner KYC documents
Bank account opening forms and source-of-funds declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional AML/KYC documentation, promptly furnish audited source-of-funds evidence or a notarial beneficial ownership statement; if a non-cash contribution is used, provide an audited valuation report in accordance with OR Article 628.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application to the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal application for registration to the Commercial Register through the official cantonal electronic register portal or paper form, accompanied by the notarially certified articles, board appointment minutes, specimen signatures, capital bank confirmation, and compliance declarations. The application must be signed by all board members and the chairperson.
required_dossiers: List of board members with specimen signatures
Declaration of compliance with Swiss capital payment rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency demand (Mängelrüge), the board must rectify the specified documentation within the set deadline, typically 30 days, or appeal through the cantonal administrative court. Late cure can require a new application with an explanatory cover letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration Fee Payment and Official Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the commercial register registration fee and the gazette publication charge. The registry transmits the registration to the SHAB for publication of the company's incorporation as required by law. Confirm the exact fee schedule with the cantonal registry before payment; retain the payment receipt for the formation file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, request written confirmation from the registry; duplicate payments are refundable, and publication errors can be rectified by a registry-generated correction notice in the SHAB.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Official Extract and Company Identification Number (UID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and Federal Statistical Office (BFS/UST) for the UID number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After final registration, obtain the official excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) showing the company's legal existence and registered details, and verify the national company identification number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, UID). The UID is assigned automatically and appears on the register extract. Ensure all registered officers and signatory powers are accurately stated.
required_dossiers: Registration confirmation from the Commercial Register Office
Valid identification for the requesting officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the register extract contains incorrect data, submit a formal correction request to the Commercial Register Office with supporting notarised evidence; the registry will issue an adjusted extract and notify the UID administration automatically.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Office for Industry and Labour (Kantonales Gewerbeamt / Arbeitsinspektorat), in coordination with the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) and Swissmedic for medical device manufacturing establishments
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial operating permission (Betriebsbewilligung / Permis d'exploiter) and Swissmedic medical device manufacturing establishment authorisation under the Swiss Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO SR 812.214)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) and the competent Cantonal Environment Protection Office (Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B screening under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (EIAO/UVPV, SR 814.11); a full EIA is not typically required for a low-volume digital X-ray detector assembly and vapour deposition line unless production capacity crosses threshold Annex I limits for chemical use, radioisotope handling, or cleanroom footprint, in which case a full EIA report is required. The operation generally qualifies for the preliminary examination/registration track.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) for industrial wastewater limits, particularly for heavy metals and cesium iodide waste; compliance with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) for volatile organic compound emission thresholds from vapour deposition and etching steps; hazardous waste handling must comply with the Waste Ordinance (VVEA) and the Chemical Risk Reduction Ordinance (ORRChem).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and fire-protection inspection under cantonal fire brigade requirements; structural load assessment for cleanroom and lead-shielding installations; occupational health clearance through the Swiss accident insurance institution (SUVA) and the Cantonal Labour Inspectorate, including workplace ventilation, radiation-safety screening for X-ray calibrators, and chemical exposure control under SUVA directives.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC), portal: www.estv.admin.ch; Swiss Business Identifier (UID) portal: www.uid.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the AG in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister) via the local commercial register office; the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX) is automatically issued and serves as the unified tax/VAT identifier. Step 2: For VAT purposes, file the mandatory VAT registration form (Berechnung der Umsätze / Déclaration de l'assujettissement) with the ESTV within 30 days of reaching the CHF 100,000 turnover threshold (Art. 10 Para 2 VAT Act). Step 3: Register for direct federal, cantonal, and communal income taxation with the competent cantonal tax administration (for Zug: Kantonales Steueramt Zug, www.zg.ch/steuern) – the AG is taxed at entity level and files annual corporate tax returns. Step 4: Apply for a Swiss customs client number (Zollkundennummer) via the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/GZD) for export procedures and electronic clearance through the Passar/NCTS system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; territorial taxation for direct taxes (Swiss-source income taxed, foreign permanent-establishment income exempt under § 52 DBG with subject-to-tax requirement); full VAT taxable-entity status for Swiss VAT purposes
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists under Swiss law; entity taxation follows statutory legal form (AG is a capital company). Available elections include: (i) participation exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains (≥10% participation or market value ≥ CHF 1 million, Art. 69/70 DBG); (ii) notional interest deduction (NID) on equity surplus in safe-harbour cantons (partial); (iii) group taxation via qualified participation election (Art. 61 DBG – consolidated profit sharing up to 3-year cycle); (iv) option to apply deemed equity taxation for principal companies in Zug; (v) VAT group election (Art. 13 VAT Act) for related Swiss entities; (vi) status of 'export trader' (HEK) for certain 0% transactions. Verification of hybrid mismatch rules is required under the Swiss implementation of BEPS Action 2 (no statutory check-the-box; alignment follows financial statement classification).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 per annum (worldwide turnover from taxable supplies and services, Art. 10 Para 2 VAT Act; goods only – threshold identical; nil for Acquirers under reverse charge on foreign digital services without local registration)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) or digital-stamping regime in Switzerland. Mandatory electronic invoicing in B2G (federal administration, eBill/Swiss QR-Invoice format since 2020). Voluntary Swiss QR-Bill invoicing standard for B2B (QR-IBAN with embedded UID and VAT pre-fill). EDI/XML structured e-invoices (E-Bilanz, Swiss EDI) are accepted as VAT-record evidence; retention obligation 10 years. No API-based clearance or digital stamping; the FOCBS mandates electronic customs declarations via the Passar (NCTS/NCTS+) system for exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies to supplies of goods transported by the seller, the buyer or a third party to a foreign destination (Art. 23 Para 1 VAT Act). Services: 0% applies to services directly related to exported goods and to certain cross-border services (Art. 23 Para 2 VAT Act), including freight, customs brokerage, quality inspection related to exported medical devices (digital X-ray flat panel detectors) and to services related to hydrology/oceanology instruments if exported. Export must be proven within a documented period (customs declaration and transport evidence); recipient must be established abroad (for services). Documentary evidence (proof of export – Ausfuhrnachweis) must be obtained by the supplier and retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung / Déclaration d'exportation) via Passar/NCTS system – with export reference number (EAN/ARN)
Bill of Lading (Ocean/Sea) or Air Waybill (AWB) – proof of cross-border transport
Commercial Invoice (with UID/VAT number of supplier and buyer, Incoterms 2020, HS code 9018.14 or 9018.90)
Internal transport evidence (CMR waybill for road, rail consignment note or logistics-company certificate of export)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/TT proof (evidence of payment received from the foreign buyer; due-diligence on FX-repatriation where required)
Customs-validated proof of exit (stamped export declaration or electronic status message from FOCBS 'Ausfuhr bestätigt')

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, acting under the National Bank Act (NBA) and the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA); supplementary enforcement by FINMA (Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority) for banking licensing and AML supervision, and by SECO for sanctions and export controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Switzerland maintains no foreign exchange control regime, no central bank approval requirement and no restriction on inward investment, profit remittance, liquidation proceeds, intercompany loans or dividend distributions. A Swiss AG distributing dividends must withhold 35% Swiss federal anticipatory tax, but the foreign shareholder may claim a full or partial refund or treaty reduction under the applicable double taxation agreement; many Swiss treaties provide a 0% rate on qualifying substantial corporate participations and 5%–15% on portfolio holdings. Repatriation of trade proceeds and debt service is unrestricted. The only administrative hurdle for non-bank enterprises is the SNB statistical declaration on forms Z1/Z2 for settlement flows with a single non-resident counterparty exceeding CHF 125,000 in a calendar month.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no export proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline and no licensing requirement for holding or disbursing foreign currency export earnings. A Swiss AG exporting DR flat-panel detectors and medical-imaging hardware may freely invoice in CHF, EUR, USD, GBP or offshore CNY and retain balances in any convertible currency. Remaining compliance duties are: (i) substantiating Swiss VAT zero-rating on exports with customs and transport documentation; (ii) reporting outbound payments on SNB form Z2 when the monthly aggregate to one non-resident counterparty exceeds CHF 125,000; and (iii) maintaining full commercial documentation to support transfer pricing and customs valuation of intra-group component flows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Gründungskonto/Sperrkonto) for the incorporation capital deposit; multi-currency Operational Account in CHF/EUR/USD/CNH after registration
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with integrated FX dealing, e-banking, and trade finance (LC/standby LC) services
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Treasury Account with strong European correspondent clearing and medical-device export experience
Operational Account on the cooperative partner-bank model; escrow account possible for the capital deposit

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank Julius Bär & Co. AG (private banking treasury platform)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for corporate treasury only where the AG forms part of a private-banking group relationship; capital escrow Account not standard

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a primary treasury substitute; Medium-to-High as a complementary payment corridor. Switzerland is outside the EU/EEA passporting system, so a UK, Lithuanian or other foreign EMI licence does not permit deposit-taking or domiciliation of Swiss corporate—only FINMA licensed Swiss payment institutions or fintech banks may hold client balances under the Swiss Banking Act (Fintech Licence, Art. 1b, currently permitting non-interest-bearing public deposits up to CHF 100 million). Funds parked with an unlicensed foreign EMI would lack Swiss depositor protection, create sanctions/AML blind spots, and jeopardise the bank confirmation needed for the incorporation capital deposit. A Swiss AG may use licensed Swiss fintechs for invoice-initiation, FX execution or EUR/USD corridor payments, while keeping the principal liquidity pool and all capital confirmation functions at a fully licensed tier-1 Swiss bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a newly incorporated Swiss AG with foreign shareholders and cross-border medical-device trading. The prevailing market standard is an in-person KYC interview at a Swiss branch involving the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one authorised signatory. Remote video identification is permitted by several tier-1 banks for low-risk structures under FINMA-approved digital onboarding procedures, but it is rarely granted where the beneficial owner is a non-resident offshore or complex-structure shareholder; in such cases banks demand in-person attendance, notarised apostilled corporate documents and a formal power of attorney. Budget accordingly for director travel to Switzerland or engagement of a Swiss domiciliation agent and independent notary to verify identity and board instructions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or shareholder is tax-resident in, or connected to, a high-risk/non-cooperative jurisdiction, or the AG shows immediate payment flows to/from such jurisdictions through intermediary trading accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence bundle: notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation and articles of association; current Zefix commercial register extract; annotated shareholder register identifying all natural persons above 10%; beneficial ownership declaration (Form A/O); source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement with audited financial statements of the shareholder; valid tax residence certificate; sanctions and PEP screening results; detailed business plan evidencing the real OEM activity in digital X-ray flat-panel detectors; bank reference from the shareholder's primary bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and immediate inbound capital injection (share capital plus shareholder loan) at incorporation flagged as capital structuring without economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes approving the capital call and shareholder loan (with arm's-length interest and repayment schedule); notarised deed evidencing the full cash payment of at least CHF 50,000 of the CHF 100,000 minimum capital; bank statement and SWIFT trail showing the funds originated from the shareholder's independently established business assets; Swiss substance proof, including registered office or lease agreement, Swiss payroll and social insurance enrolment, and capex/opex budget for the DR detector production and procurement activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound trade payments to component suppliers or distributors in sensitive geographies (e.g., amorphous-silicon TFT foundries, cesium-iodide scintillator vendors, electronics OEM subcontractors) triggering sanctions and transaction-monitoring alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade-file package: executed master supply contract with Incoterms; proforma and commercial invoices; packing lists; air/sea waybills and customs declarations; export certificates; HS code classification (e.g., 9022.14 for X-ray equipment); regulatory file (CE/FDA/ISO 13485 as applicable); UCP600 documentary credit draft or SWIFT MT103 with full remittance references; explanation of any third-party payment instruction; KYB refreshes and end-beneficiary confirmations for each material supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque multi-tier holding chain, nominee shareholder arrangements, trusts or discretionary vehicles concealing the true ownership of the AG.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transparent group and control chart traced to ultimate natural persons; notarised declaration by all directors and shareholders of their beneficial ownership; trust deed or fiduciary declaration where applicable; registration of the AG in the Swiss beneficial-ownership transparency register; consolidated audited financial statements of the parent group; bank references and regulatory status confirmation of the parent group; undertaking to notify any change in control within statutory deadlines.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The CHF 100,000 minimum share capital of the AG (at least CHF 50,000 effectively paid-in in cash under Art. 632 of the Swiss Code of Obligations) must be deposited on a dedicated capital escrow account at a Swiss bank before registration. Compliant routing: non-resident shareholder executes an SWIFT MT103 in CHF or a freely convertible currency to the bank account in the exact name of the AG, with remittance information (field 70) clearly stating 'Anzahlung auf das Aktienkapital – Einlage in das Aktienkapital' and identifying the payor and company. The receiving bank issues a capital-payment confirmation (Kapitalbestätigung/Einlagebestätigung) used by the notary and Commercial Register Office. After registration, the board releases the funds to the operational account. No SNB approval is required. Inbound receipts from a single non-resident counterparty above CHF 125,000 per calendar month must be captured in the enterprise's SNB Z1 statistical report. If the injection is routed through an intermediate third-country bank, the SWIFT ordering-account data must show the ultimate originator and source of funds; otherwise the transfer may be frozen pending enhanced due diligence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for DR detector component procurement (amorphous-silicon layers, cesium-iodide scintillators, TFT arrays, aluminium/glass substrates and electronics) are executed on the Swiss operational account through: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfers with invoice/P.O. references in the remittance field for T/T suppliers; (2) documentary letters of credit (MT700) issued under UCP600 through the bank's trade finance desk, enabling secure payment against presentation of transport documents and commonly confirmed by Asian advising banks; (3) standby letters of credit (MT760) or demand guarantees securing milestone prepayments to OEM subcontractors; and (4) SEPA Credit Transfers for EUR-denominated payments to EU suppliers, Switzerland being a participating SEPA country. All outbound flows exceeding CHF 125,000 per calendar month to a single non-resident counterparty are reported on SNB form Z2. Each payment must be reconciled against the underlying commercial contract, export/import documentation and transfer-pricing file to withstand OECD and Swiss tax audit scrutiny.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (tenors 1–24 months) in EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, GBP/CHF and CNH/CHF settled OTC under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's Swiss Master Agreement for FX derivatives with a collateralised CSA credit support annex.
FX swaps (spot/forward pairs) for short-term treasury liquidity conversion between CHF, EUR and USD, including principal exchange at inception and re-exchange at maturity.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) and long-dated FX forwards to hedge shareholder loans, project capex financing or multi-year OEM supply contracts where the exposure is in USD or EUR against CHF.
OTC European-style FX options (calls and puts) on EUR/USD, USD/CHF and EUR/CHF for budget rate insurance and margin protection, subject to FIDLEG suitability and documentation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted strictly to non-deliverable emerging-market supply-chain currencies where the underlying is not freely convertible (e.g., certain Asian and CEEMEA exotic currencies); NDFs are not necessary for CHF, EUR or USD pairs, which are fully deliverable, and any NDF requires separate bank credit approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and adoption of the statutory annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders (internal corporate organ); minutes and the approved accounts are retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date (Art. 699 para. 2 CO); for a 31 December year-end, the AGM must be held by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A shareholder may obtain a court order convening the AGM; the Board faces civil liability for delays; continued failure to appoint required corporate organs permits the commercial register to order dissolution ex officio (Art. 731b CO).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (federal, cantonal and municipal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung), with the federal corporate income tax assessed through the same single-window return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the fiscal year-end; calendar-year AG files by 30 June; up to six months' extension generally granted on written or electronic request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% p.a. (federal) and 4%-5% p.a. (cantonal); a procedural fine of up to CHF 10,000 for intent and CHF 2,000 for negligence under cantonal tax law; ex officio assessment with a substantial surcharge; tax evasion penalties up to three times the tax initially evaded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the VAT period; with annual filing privilege, the return for a calendar-year company is due by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at approximately 4.5% p.a.; procedural penalties up to CHF 8,000; where input-tax deductions and refunds are unsupported, assessments are revised and recoverable with penalty; deliberate evasion triggers surcharges of up to three times the tax avoided and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register mutations and continuity filings (directors, auditor, registered office, share capital, branches)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / registre du commerce) at the AG's statutory seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the corporate resolution for most mutations; Swiss law imposes event-driven filings rather than a general annual return; the register's factual accuracy must be maintained at all times
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registration office may order compliance with fines up to CHF 5,000 (Art. 943 CO); if an AG is without a valid board, auditor, or registered address, the register publishes a default notice and may strike the company off the register (Art. 934a CO, Art. 153 ff. HRegV).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO / beneficial-ownership register annual verification and declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company internal AML/UBO register, verified annually at the AGM; Federal UBO registry filings to be triggered upon qualifying ownership changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediate update upon share transfers or control changes; annual confirmation of the beneficial-ownership schedule embedded in the AGM discharge process; no recurring federal filing is required for an unchanged shareholding structure of a private AG
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Swiss anti-money-laundering criminal provisions (Art. 41-44 AMLA) up to CHF 500,000 for serious infractions; directors face civil liability for deficiencies; negligent omission of UBO documentation may invalidate the annual discharge and expose the entity to due-diligence referrals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit under Art. 727 CO is mandatory when the AG is exchange-listed, when a special law regulates its audit, or when the AG exceeds two of the following three thresholds during two consecutive fiscal years: (i) balance-sheet total of CHF 20 million or more; (ii) annual sales revenue of CHF 40 million or more; (iii) annual average of 250 or more full-time employees. Below those thresholds a limited audit (eingeschränkte Revision) is the default, waivable only if the AG employs on annual average fewer than 10 full-time employees and all shareholders consent to the waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory reporting under the Swiss Code of Obligations (Arts. 957-963f CO); IFRS acceptable and required only for certain consolidated/listed group statements; Swiss GAAP FER may be voluntarily applied as a recognized true-and-fair framework; the annual report must be prepared within six months and adopted by the AGM; business books and vouchers must be retained for 10 years (Art. 958f CO).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The board must know and record every beneficial owner holding more than 25% of the share capital or control, directly or indirectly, in the internal UBO list; each share transfer is entered without delay, and the schedule is formally verified at every AGM; where the ownership structure is unchanged, Swiss law does not impose a separate public annual UBO declaration for a non-listed private AG, but any qualifying change is reportable to the Federal UBO registry within the applicable statutory window once the transparency regime applies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder register / Aktienregister) for registered shares
Register of Directors and signatory-authorization register
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board minutes
Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO list under Swiss AML regulation)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 680 - 3,400 per annum (CHF 600 - 3,000) for Swiss law-licensed registered-office and corporate agent services, typically USD 1,100 for an SME AG without banking-consortium complexity
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 16,000 per annum for the statutory limited audit (CHF 5,000 - 14,000); USD 15,000 - 45,000 per annum if an ordinary audit (Revisionsstelle) becomes compulsory under the Art. 727 CO thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory flat tax 8.5% on net accounting profit before federal tax, which yields an effective federal burden of 7.83% on pre-tax profit because the federal tax itself is deductible. Combined federal + cantonal + communal headline rate in Zug (Crypto Valley prevailing jurisdiction) is approximately 11.9%, one of the lowest in Switzerland; high-tax cantons such as Geneva and Zurich reach approximately 14.0% and 21.0% respectively.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss tax reform effective 2020 abolished privileged domiciliary/holding statuses and introduced: (i) patent box deduction of up to 90% of qualifying IP income (only 10% of the net royalty/patent profit is taxable); (ii) R&D super-deduction of up to 150% of qualifying R&D costs in cantons that enacted it, including Zurich and Geneva; (iii) cantonal innovation tax holidays for newly created manufacturing or high-tech ventures for up to 10 years in certain cantons; (iv) notional interest deduction on excessive equity in cantons that adopted it (e.g. Zurich, Geneva); (v) federal/cantonal participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from shareholdings of at least 10% held for at least 12 months. The OECD GloBE/Pillar Two 15% minimum rate applies to the group if consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Steuererklärung juristische Personen (Mantel-/B-Formular), a unified federal-cantonal annual corporate tax return for Aktiengesellschaften, filed electronically through the Zug canton eTax portal (eTax Zug) or approved SWISS tax software transmitted to the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV); the separate annual withholding-tax declaration on Form 710 (Verrechnungssteuer-Erklärung) must accompany transfer of Swiss dividends and bond interest.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; preliminary quarterly tax installments based on prior-year assessed profit are due on 15 February, 15 May, 15 August and 15 November; the return is filed once per fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Where the statutory fiscal year is 1 January to 31 December, the return is due by 31 March of the following year in Zug, with a customary extension to 30 September upon request; where a non-calendar business year is used, the due date is six months after the balance-sheet date; the federal return deadline is aligned with the cantonal deadline, and the assessed tax is payable 30 days after the writ of assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 101 - Entity Information (UID, VAT, Registered Office, Board)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Swiss UID (canton Zug tax number), VAT number, legal form 'Aktiengesellschaft', registered seat, purpose clause concentrated on medical imaging hardware, board of directors, authorized signatories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG is the sole taxpayer; a non-resident shareholder has no Swiss annual filing obligation for the AG return; appoint a Swiss-resident registered office and, where the board is non-resident, a formal Swiss tax representative with power of attorney.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the Swiss taxation/reporting period; must reconcile with the audited IFRS/Swiss GAAP FER financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the standard 1 January - 31 December period for alignment with the Zug calendar-year tax cycle; a separate parent-company fiscal year does not alter the Swiss deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current and non-current assets: cash, trade receivables, inventory of amorphous silicon and cesium iodide imaging panels, production equipment, tooling, and capitalized intangible property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The asset base must be supported by the transfer-pricing Local File; AG assets in Switzerland indicate substance; no foreign assets of the non-resident parent are reportable in Switzerland unless disposed through a Swiss permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross invoiced turnover from OEM sales of digital X-ray flat-panel detectors, after-sales service contracts, spare parts and calibration services, net of discounts and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Export sales to related-persons are reported at Swiss arm's-length revenue; the chosen TNMM/CUP pricing policy must be contemporaneously documented; advance pricing agreements are available from the FTA Grand Billing department.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: salaries and Swiss social security contributions, clean-room material costs, depreciation, utilities, insurance, R&D expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign secondees working in Switzerland trigger Swiss PAYE and AHV; any management fee to the foreign parent is deductible only if supported by a service agreement and arm's-length mark-up under the Cost Plus method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit of the AG per Swiss Code of Obligations prior to any tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax return starts from this line; the FTA may add back non-deductible expenses, excessive director compensation, constructive dividends, or non-arms-length intercompany charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal and cantonal taxable profit after steuerliche Korrekturen: reversal of excessive provisions, depreciation range adjustments, disallowed M&A costs, and correction of hidden distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review constructive-dividend exposure where Swiss AG sells panels to the non-resident parent/affiliate below open-market value or receives IP royalties above CUP; any under-pricing is re-characterized as dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for exemption of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from a foreign or Swiss subsidiary shareholding of at least 10% held for at least 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support with a shareholding register of the AG; foreign withholding taxes on the underlying dividend are not taken into account in Switzerland; treaty due-diligence documentation should nonetheless be maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of all cross-border controlled transactions, the entities involved, the prices charged, and the arm's-length method applied (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split), with reference to the Local File and group Master File.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG must show a benchmarked operating margin for its OEM manufacturing functions; where the foreign parent provides IP, a lump-sum royalty license must be priced on a CUP basis; the parent may not appropriate Swiss residual profit without tax base erosion consequences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 700 - Withholding-Tax Credits and Refund Claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Swiss 35% Verrechnungssteuer withheld on bank interest, bond interest and dividends is reclaimable or creditable by the AG; foreign tax credits for underlying WHT on foreign royalties/interest may also be claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not enter this schedule for the dividend paid by the AG; they must apply separately for DTA relief through Form 821/8200 with their tax residence certificate within three years of the payment date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Signature Block - CEO / CFO / Tax Representative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of completeness and truthfulness under criminal penalty; Swiss tax representative countersignature required where no resident board member is authorized.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide an irrevocable power of attorney to a licensed Swiss fiduciary; the non-resident CEO's signature legally binds the AG but does not allow the representative to be bypassed for service of process.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers, in order: automated reminder; formal order with threat of fine; the Zug tax authority may assess the AG by estimation on the basis of prior-year results and bank data; procedural non-compliance fines of up to CHF 10,000 per federal and cantonal level (Art. 174 DBG); default interest on unpaid tax at 4.5% per annum accruing from 1 February of the year following the tax year; intentional failure to file or materially incomplete filing qualifies as tax evasion, with fines up to 250% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of responsible directors for up to 3 years under Art. 186 DBG.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividend distributions by the AG; Switzerland levies no cantonal or communal withholding tax on dividends; the DTA generally reduces the rate to 0% for qualifying substantial corporate shareholdings (typically 10% to 25% depending on treaty), to 5% for portfolio corporate investors, and to 15% for individuals; a refund of the excess withheld must be requested within 3 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Administrative protocol: (1) verify treaty entitlement and that the divided-receiving shareholder is the beneficial owner with substance; (2) obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) for the fiscal year of the payment from the shareholder's tax authority (e.g. IRS Form 6166 for the US, Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung for Germany); (3) either apply for advance relief before the dividend is paid (Vorgängiges Entlastungsverfahren using Form 8206, with the FTA issuing an authorization to the paying agent to withhold at the reduced rate), or pay the 35% and file Form 821 (Erstattungsantrag) with the ESTV within three years from the payment due date; (4) attach the shareholder register extract proving the minimum shareholding percentage and holding period; (5) carry out a Substance / Limitation-on-Benefits self-check because Swiss treaty relief is denied to shell companies and to hybrid mismatches. Claims of less than CHF 1,500 follow a simplified electronic procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: the Swiss domestic statutory rate is 35%, but only on bond issues ('Obligationen') and similar marketable debt instruments; ordinary cross-border intercompany loans and bank financing sourced outside a public Swiss bond issuance are exempt from Swiss withholding tax; DTA rates are typically 0% to 10% (e.g. under the Switzerland-US DTA the 35% domestic rate drops to 0% on commercial loans). Royalties: Switzerland imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalty payments under domestic law; the gross amount can be paid without Swiss tax deduction; inbound royalty income received by the Swiss AG is taxable at ordinary corporate rates but may benefit from the Swiss patent box leaving only 10% of the qualifying royalty profit effectively taxable; treaty rates for royalties to/from Swiss residents are commonly 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File / TP documentation threshold (Art. 1 TDok-V): a Swiss company must prepare a Local File when it has annual gross turnover above CHF 100 million and carries out cross-border transactions with related parties; the Master File must be prepared when the parent group has consolidated gross turnover above CHF 1 billion; simplified documentation applies for qualifying SMEs with gross revenue below CHF 10 million or where group cross-border revenue is below CHF 5 million; documentation must be submitted within 60 days of the FTA's written request and must be in German, French or English.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing regime. Economic substance is nevertheless indispensable and is enforced indirectly through: (i) Swiss treaty anti-abuse and PPT/LOB clauses, which require substantial business activity, premises, employees and entrepreneurial risk in Switzerland; (ii) the 2020 tax reform, which abolished the privileged treatment of domiciliary/holding companies; (iii) Art. 58a DBG anti-deferral rules targeting the transfer of taxable assets to low-tax jurisdictions; and (iv) the beneficial-ownership condition in the Swiss withholding-tax refund process. For the digital X-ray detector manufacturing AG, on-site production, clean-room assets, R&D staffing and qualified management must be documented because the FTA will test economic substance when a transfer-pricing adjustment, DTA relief claim or APA application is filed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful or grossly negligent omission of taxable revenue, overstatement of raw-material inventory, falsified export invoices, concealed bank accounts of the AG, or understated share capital; the AG files a materially incorrect tax return showing lower Swiss taxable profit and obtains an under-assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty equal to 25%-250% of the evaded tax (federal, Art. 175-176 DBG), plus 4.5% per annum default interest; criminal prosecution results in a fine up to CHF 250,000 and/or imprisonment for responsible managers for up to 3 years (Art. 186 DBG); in aggravated cases with forged books the Swiss Criminal Code money-laundering and forgery provisions may add imprisonment up to 10 years; the tax shortfall remains fully recoverable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the false return are joint and several obligors for the civil tax surcharge under Art. 754(1) CO; the FTA may issue a personal liability order against the CFO/CEO when the company becomes insolvent; the criminal court may order a travel ban, confiscation of unlawfully retained gains, and the responsible foreign directors are extraditable under the bilateral extradition treaties; custodial sentences of up to 3 years apply.
